item.title: ▶ Can you swap white rice without giving up rice completely or wasting money on expensive “diabetic rice”? ...
item.dc:creator: Monitor Munchies · Instagram
item.description:
Can you swap white rice without giving up rice completely or wasting money on expensive “diabetic rice”?
I put 200g of Brown Basmati Rice (with 30g spicy lentil powder) to the test using my Dexcom CGM, and the results were surprising! Even with zero physical activity after eating, the spike was almost 50% lower than white rice with a smooth, steady curve and no crash. Watch the video to see the exact peak rise!
Why does this work? The intact brown bran layer packs natural fiber, and Basmati is naturally high in slow-digesting amylose starch. Together, they slow down digestion for a gradual glucose release, sustained energy, and better long-term insulin sensitivity.
Stop spending big money on overpriced “diabetic rice” full of false promises! Stay tuned: my very next video is a real CGM test on diabetic rice itself.
Share this with friends and family who love rice and want to eat smarter!
(Note: I run these tests multiple times under controlled conditions with no post-meal activity to ensure accuracy. Individual responses vary, esp to those with medical conditions. This content is for informational purposes only and is not medical advice.)
#BrownBasmatiRice #BloodSugarControl #CGMExperiment #EatSmart #weightlossjournal

item.title: 🇮🇳 DID YOU KNOW THE WORD “SUGAR” HAS INDIAN ROOTS?...
item.dc:creator: Monitor Munchies · Instagram
item.description:
🇮🇳 DID YOU KNOW THE WORD “SUGAR” HAS INDIAN ROOTS?

Long before the world called it Sugar, ancient India had a Sanskrit word: Śarkarā (शर्करा).

Originally meaning gravel or small crystals, Śarkarā also came to describe crystalline sugar.

As sugar and its name traveled across civilizations, the word evolved:

🇮🇳 India (Sanskrit): Śarkarā
🇮🇷 Persia: Shakar
🌙 Arabic: Sukkar
🏛️ Medieval Latin: Succarum
🇫🇷 France: Sucre
🇬🇧 English: Sugar

Different languages. Different civilizations. One fascinating Indian linguistic root!

India played a pioneering role in the history of sugar, particularly in developing methods of crystallizing it.

But here’s the irony. 💔

The same India that contributed so much to the world’s sugar history is now facing an enormous metabolic health crisis.

Today, India has approximately 90 million adults living with diabetes, the second-highest number in the world.

We have every reason to celebrate our history, but also every reason to protect our future.

❤️ We gave the world a word for sugar. Let’s not let sugar-related health problems define our future.

This isn’t about fearing sugar. It’s about understanding nutrition, making informed choices, staying active, and protecting our metabolic health.

🇮🇳 Let’s be remembered for our contribution to sugar’s history, not for the burden of metabolic disease.

🌿 Monitor Munchies
Let’s all eat smart.

#MonitorMunchies #SugarHistory #MetabolicHealth #DiabetesAwareness #EatSmart

item.title: ▶ Maggi Noodles and Blood Sugar. How fast does our favorite 2-minute comfort food actually spike glucose…
item.dc:creator: Monitor Munchies · Instagram
item.description:
Maggi Noodles and Blood Sugar. How fast does our favorite 2-minute comfort food actually spike glucose when eaten on an empty stomach?
Most people reach for instant noodles for a quick, convenient meal, but ultra-processed refined maida, palm oil, high sodium, and synthetic taste enhancers hit your bloodstream rapidly with almost zero fiber to slow digestion down.
In today’s experiment, I cooked 2 cakes of Maggi in the original style and ate it as my first meal on an empty stomach using my Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM). Every test in this series is performed multiple times with zero physical activity after the meal to give you accurate, real-world metabolic data.
How does it compare to the other junk foods I’ve tested like Thumbs Up and French Fries?
Let’s just say… this glucose rollercoaster is one you’ll want to see for yourself.
Watch the full reel to see what the CGM revealed, and explore my Reels section to check out my past junk food and breakfast experiments!
Let’s all eat smart.
Disclaimer: This content is based on my personal Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) experiments and is shared for educational and informational purposes only… it is not medical advice. The graph and data shown are original Monitor Munchies test results and are strictly for personal viewing; please do not reproduce, share, or reuse without permission. For illustration only. Curves are normalized; actual glucose levels and timing differ. Based on my personal CGM readings.
